title: Belladonna of Sadness and 70's Hippie counter-culture

commenti.body:
I have nothing interesting to say about Belladonna but I want to say that anime and animation in general is in dire of need of a cultural, intellectual revaluation and having its status in the canon of cinema fixed.
I get the feeling that like in the 20th century when people cared about art, and the canons were being established, people generally saw animation as a children’s meduim and I think taht stigma still has effects today.
 There was this whole movement of animation happening in Japan filled with talented artists that took animation and filmmaking in all kind of new and groundbreaking directions, that never got as much spotlight as they deserved.
You can’t find much academic discussion about anime and it’s hard to filter out the art from the commercial disposable otaku content that surrounds it, so films like Belladonna of Sadness, Ghost Ship, Angel’s Egg are relegated to being talked about in niche elitist circles within an already niche hobby.
All this to say, the issue you bring up about the prelevant dicussion of a certain piece completely misunderstanding the film is more common than you think simply because I beleive not enough people with sufficient background in art literacy have weighed in on these pieces.

I don’t know, I am drunk, perhaps I am reading too much into it, perhaps anime is just a small kitsch movement that doesn’t deserve much recognition, perhaps Mamoro Oshii shouldn’t be put next to Riddley Scott but these have been some ideas that pop into my mind every so often.
